headline: Kobe Sanders scored nine points (2-of-7 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs) with four rebounds, three steals and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers.
body: With Rui Hachimura (quad) sidelined, the Clippers turned to Sanders to fill the void in the starting lineup. Beyond the steals, the production on Wednesday was limited. Sanders should only be rostered in extremely deep redraft leagues and dynasty leagues, even if Hachimura can’t play on Friday against the Timberwolves.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Darius Garland finished Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers with 14 points (4-of-12 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), one rebound, five assists, one steal and one three-pointer.
body: While Garland is shooting a respectable 46.3 percent from the field, turnovers have hurt his early-season value in nine-cat leagues. He committed five turnovers against the Lakers and is now averaging 5.8 per game. In four games, Garland has 26 assists and 21 turnovers. To be fair to Garland, he’s been playing through back tightness, according to Clippers head coach Tyronn Lue. And the hard fall he took on a layup attempt during the second half of Wednesday’s game didn’t help. Injuries have limited the Clippers’ rotation, and that may also explain Garland’s high turnover count.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Derrick Jones Jr. produced 15 points (6-of-10 FGs), five rebounds, four steals, two blocks and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers.
body: Rostered in just 12 percent of Yahoo leagues, Jones is undervalued in category leagues. Against the Lakers, he recorded six “stocks” and shot 60 percent from the field. He’s now 10-of-18 from beyond the arc in four games. Will Jones sustain his current percentages from the field (57.6) and beyond the arc? Probably not. That said, he’s worth rostering while the Clippers await the returns of Brandon Ingram and Max Strus.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Keaton Wagler accounted for 21 points (4-of-15 FGs, 10-of-12 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers.
body: A double-digit scorer in each of his first three regular-season games, Wagler finished Wednesday’s defeat with his first 20-point game. The rookie took advantage of the foul line against the Lakers, scoring 10 of his 21 points at the charity stripe. However, Wagler continues to struggle from the field, shooting 31.6 percent. The good news for fantasy managers is that he’s found other ways to provide value, making him a player worth rostering for those willing to take the field-goal percentage hit.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Sandro Mamukelashvili tallied 13 points (6-of-15 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
body: After totaling 21 points in the Lakers’ first three games, Mamukelashvili has hit double figures in each of his last two. Against the Clippers, his perimeter shot wasn’t falling, as he missed all five three-point attempts. But Mamu was 6-of-10 from two, and he did a little of everything else. Despite the bench role, Mamukelasvhili is worth rostering in deep leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Quentin Grimes accumulated 23 points (7-of-15 FGs, 9-of-11 FTs), three rebounds, five assists and four steals in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
body: Grimes replaced the injured Luka Dončić (back) in the starting lineup on Wednesday, and he was excellent. He led all scorers with 23 points and added some assists and steals. Grimes shot 0-of-3 from beyond the arc, but he was over 50 percent from two. Even in his usual reserve role, Grimes is worth rostering in deeper leagues because the Lakers need scorers beyond Dončić and Austin Reaves, and he can fill that role.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kingston Flemings had 23 points (9-of-12 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers against the Heat on Wednesday.
body: Flemings came off the bench, played 28 minutes and had the best game of his young career so far. The 19-year-old rookie was impressive with 23 points on 12 attempts from the field and a full stat line. Flemings ended up playing more minutes than starter CJ McCollum, but don’t expect that to continue. Timing Flemings’ next outstanding performance will be difficult given his inconsistent playing time, making him more of a priority in dynasty formats.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Matisse Thybulle amassed 15 points (5-of-6 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), one rebound, two steals, one block and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
body: Entering Wednesday, Thybulle was shooting 42.1 percent from three. His 4-of-5 night against the Clippers will increase that percentage, and fantasy managers can also benefit from the defensive stats. Given his play so far and the starting role, Thybulle should be rostered in deeper fantasy leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Austin Reaves accounted for 16 points (6-of-16 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, one assist, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
body: The Lakers didn’t have Luka Dončić (back) on Wednesday, with his absence shifting Reaves into the starting point guard role. Unfortunately for fantasy managers hoping for more production from Reaves, it didn’t happen. More damaging than the field-goal percentage was the turnover count, as he racked up eight. The good news is that the Lakers play two more games in Week 2, starting with the Warriors on Friday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Collin Sexton finished Wednesday’s win over the Clippers with 21 points (6-of-11 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and four three-pointers.
body: In his first three games this season, Sexton totaled 27 points on 11-of-28 shooting from the field. With Luka Dončić (back) out, Sexton didn’t move into the starting lineup, but his playmaking role off the bench became even more important on Wednesday. The veteran guard shot over 50 percent from the field overall and 4-of-7 from three in his best performance of the season to date. While he hasn’t been consistent enough to merit a roster spot in 12-team leagues, Sexton is worth considering in deeper leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: RJ Barrett with a monster 25 points (9-of-8 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), nine rebounds, six assists, a steal and three 3-pointers on Wednesday against the Magic.
body: RJ Barrett took the shots early in this game in the first game without Kawhi and was efficient from the field. Notably, he was on the exercise bike at multiple points in this game, so it could be something to monitor. If you got RJ Barrett in fantasy, you should be really happy about what he’s been doing. He won’t get you many defensive numbers but he will certainly score, and get you some rebounds. There’s an opportunity with Kawhi out, so there could be room to sell-high if someone gives you a good offer.

headline: Scottie Barnes has 28 points (11-of-17 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, four assists, three steals, and two blocks in 129-99 win against the Magic.
body: With no Kawhi Leonard, Scottie Barnes made up the difference and kept the defense aggressive in this game. He’s very good as a roamer and can get a lot of his defensive numbers that way. If you drafted Scottie Barnes, you should be feeling very happy about that decision and should be in contention to finish in the top 10 of fantasy rankings this season.

headline: Nickeil Alexander-Walker had 23 points (8-of-18 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, one assist, one steal and five three-pointers against the Heat on Wednesday.
body: Alexander-Walker led the Hawks with 23 points, breaking a stretch of three consecutive games where he fell short of at least 20 points. He’s made at least four three-pointers in three of five games so far this season. Alexander-Walker averaged a career-high 3.2 made three-pointers per game last season and he’s carried his outside shooting success into this year.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jase Richardson got 10 points (4-of-8 FGs), a rebound, an assist, and two 3-pointers in start against Raptors.
body: Even though he started, Jase didn’t end up playing starters minutes. After playing the first four minutes, he didn’t return to the game until the third quarter since the Magic needed more size to match against Toronto. In college he was known as a connective glue guy while being efficient, and that’s exactly what he’s done up to this point. In dynasty, the ceiling will depend on how much of a scorer and shooter he can be, because it’s getting harder to play at his size if he’s not a PG, which he really isn’t.

headline: Desmond Bane put up 13 points (3-of-14 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, four assists, a steal, two blocks, and two 3-pointers in 99-129 loss to Raptors.
body: It was a bad night for Bane as he couldn’t get shots to fall against the Raptors. Bane in the past two seasons has shot 48.4% from the field, but he hasn’t shot very well this season. There is a good track record to indicate that there will be a bounce back from Bane and to not panic too much about his efficiency. He at least got you five rebounds and four assists to give you some value.

headline: Franz Wagner had 15 points (4-of-11 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, and seven turnovers in blowout loss to Raptors.
body: Franz was one of the only players that could get shots up in this game. The Magic struggled with efficiency as they dealt with the Raptors aggressive defense, but you can see it affected Franz with the 7 turnovers. The Magic will play the Raptors again on Friday and will get a second chance at redemption where he will look to have a better performance.

headline: Kelly Oubre with 15 points (5-of-10 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, an assist, and a three taking over Haliburton in the starting lineup.
body: With no Haliburton and Zubac tonight, Oubre’s scoring was much needed in the Pacers come back. From a fantasy perspective, he doesn’t provide much outside of decent scoring and occasional rebounding, so he’s fine if you need a boost in those categories, but he will have other games where the shot isn’t there and there’s not a lot there from a fantasy perspective.

headline: Pascal Siakam had a monster 26 points (11-of-17 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), 11 rebounds, three assists, and a steal on Wednesday.
body: Pascal did his best to lead the Pacers without Haliburton in this game and did a good job scoring the ball. He was a monster on the boards as the Pacers out hustled the 76ers in this game. We have at least two weeks before Haliburton comes back, so sit back and enjoy the production but also recognize that it might come down a bit once Haliburton comes back.

headline: Jordan Poole (ankle) will not return against the Nuggets on Wednesday.
body: Poole hurt himself on a transition layup attempt. If Poole were to miss some time, look for more minutes for Bennedict Mathurin and Herb Jones. Bryce McGowens could also get into the rotation as a backup guard.

headline: Yanic Konan Niederhäuser (foot) will not travel with the Clippers for their upcoming two-game road trip.
body: Niederhäuser is working his way back from a Lisfranc injury that ended his rookie season in early March. He’s progressing in his recovery, and the team has decided he will stay home to continue that process rather than travel with the Clippers for road games on Friday and Sunday. Thus far, the Clippers have relied mainly on Isaiah Jackson and Brook Lopez at center, with rookie Baba Miller getting a few minutes as well.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Max Strus (foot) will remain in Los Angeles to continue his rehab instead of traveling with the Clippers for their upcoming road trip.
body: Strus, who injured his right foot in an early-October preseason game, is scheduled for re-evaluation in a week. Instead of traveling with the team for road games on Friday and Sunday, he’ll stay in Los Angeles to continue his rehab work. Given the timeline provided at the beginning of the month, Strus’ return to the court may not be far away.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Brandon Ingram (Achilles) will not travel with the Clippers for their upcoming road trip.
body: Following Wednesday’s home game against the Lakers, the Clippers will play their next two on the road. Ingram is progressing in his recovery from a partially torn Achilles, but he will remain in Los Angeles to continue his rehab.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Utah Jazz will start Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson, Josh Green, Ace Bailey, and Jaxson Hayes against the Spurs.
body: Josh Green will start in place of Lauri Markkanen tonight who is out with a wrist injury, and Jaxson Hayes will return to the starting lineup for the injured Jaren Jackson Jr. Green and Hayes can be used as streamers but neither will be factors in most redraft leagues. Look for Darryn and Ace to pick up the scoring in this game.

headline: Jaxson Hayes (shoulder) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Spurs.
body: Hayes is back after sitting out Monday’s loss to the Grizzlies with a sore right shoulder. With Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. out, he may start on Wednesday. Hayes isn’t the most reliable fantasy option, but the opportunity makes him worthy of a look in deep leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Lauri Markkanen (wrist) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Spurs.
body: Markkanen is dealing with a sprained right wrist that he suffered Monday against the Grizzlies. Without Markkanen, Kyle Filipowski figures to see enough minutes to make him a worthwhile streamer.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Ajay Mitchell (ankle) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Mavericks.
body: Initially questionable for Wednesday’s game, Mitchell is now available. Because of Oklahoma City’s injuries, he should be rostered in most redraft leagues. Mitchell is coming off his first 30-point game in Monday’s win over the Suns.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jamal Murray, Christian Braun, Aaron Gordon, Trevon Brazile and Nikola Jokić will start Wednesday’s game against the Pelicans.
body: Brazile has gotten off to a good start in his rookie season, and he’s been rewarded with a spot in Wednesday’s starting lineup. He replaces fellow rookie Bryce Hopkins, who started Denver’s last two games.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Naji Marshall (illness) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Thunder.
body: Marshall is officially out after the Mavericks downgraded him to doubtful on Wednesday afternoon. This will be the second straight game he’s missed, and players like Walter Clayton Jr. and Caleb Martin could absorb the available minutes.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: The Toronto Raptors will start Immanuel Quickley, Ja’Kobe Walter, RJ Barrett, Scottie Barnes, and Jakob Poeltl against the Magic on Friday.
body: Kawhi Leonard is out with knee soreness, so Ja’Kobe Walter will get the start against the Magic. He’s useful if you need some points and 3’s but he likely will not be much more than a deeper league guy. Look for Barnes, Quickley, and Barrett to pick up the slack without Kawhi. Immanuel Quickley RJ Barrett Scottie Barnes Jakob Poeltl

headline: Jase Richardson, Desmond Bane, Anthony Black, Franz Wagner and Wendell Carter Jr. will start Wednesday’s game against the Raptors.
body: Already without Paolo Banchero, the Magic lost Jalen Suggs (knee) during Sunday’s win over the Knicks. His absence pushes Black into the starting lineup. Also, Richardson remains in the starting lineup, but those who added Tristan da Silva recently shouldn’t worry, as he’ll play plenty.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cameron Johnson (ankle) will not play on Wednesday against the Pelicans.
body: Cameron Johnson will miss another game with an ankle injury. Spencer Jones has also been out which has allowed second round pick rookie Bryce Hopkins to get two consecutive starts. Johnson will have another opportunity to suit up against the Suns on Friday.

headline: Ayo Dosunmu will be the starter in place of Anthony Edwards.
body: This was the expected outcome given that he’s the backup two guard. Ayo recently signed a 5 year/112M dollar contract this off-season to return to the Timberwolves after his performance in the playoffs. In fantasy leagues, Dosunmu isn’t the most category friendly player, but he’s a player that can get you some points, some 3’s and some decent rebounds and assists. If he isn’t grabbed in your leagues, he’s worth a look.

headline: Gui Santos (knee) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Timberwolves.
body: Santos has unsurprisingly been ruled out after popping up on the injury report hours before the game with left knee tendonitis. Georges Niang and Al Horford are candidates to start are see more minutes with Santos sidelined, though neither are worth streaming consideration in most fantasy leagues.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Ausar Thompson (ankle) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Hornets.
body: Thompson was initially probable for Wednesday’s game, so the status upgrade is unsurprising. The Pistons will stick with the five that started Tuesday’s loss to the Knicks, with Cade Cunningham, Duncan Robinson, John Collins and Paul Reed rounding out the quintet.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Indiana Pacers will start Andrew Nembhard, Kelly Oubre Jr., Aaron Smith, Pascal Siakam, and Jay Huff against the 76ers on Wednesday.
body: Kelly Oubre will step in as the starter with Tyrese Haliburton being ruled out for a couple weeks due to a hamstring injury and Andrew Nembhard will shift to the the full time point guard spot. Oubre could take on more usage in Haliburton’s absence, but Nembhard is the first guy to look at.

headline: Gui Santos (knee) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Timberwolves.
body: Santos popped up on the injury report as questionable with left knee tendonitis, which typically isn’t a great sign for one’s availability. Georges Niang and Al Horford are potential candidates to start if Santos is ultimately ruled out Wednesday.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown, LeBron James and Joel Embiid will start Wednesday’s game against the Pacers.
body: Embiid and Edgecombe are back after sitting out Sunday’s loss to the Pistons. As a result, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Dean Wade will come off the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Nic Claxton (hamstring) getting closer to return.
body: Head coach Tiago Splitter said Claxton will likely travel with the team for their upcoming road trip as he is progressing from his injury. Fantasy managers should keep an eye on updates, but Jalen Smith will be the starting center until Claxton returns.
author: Shawn Robinson

headline: Aaron Nesmith (hamstring) is now questionable for Wednesday’s game against the 76ers.
body: Initially probable for Wednesday night, Nesmith’s status has been downgraded. Given the absences the Pacers already face, most notably Tyrese Haliburton, losing another starter would be suboptimal. Whether he starts or stays on the bench, Jarace Walker should get more opportunities if Nesmith can’t play.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Pacers coach Rick Carlisle told reporters Ben Sheppard (knee) will be out for months.
body: Sheppard underwent surgery for a torn meniscus last week and it was revealed that he needed a full repair. Carlisle said that while there’s currently no timetable for his return, Sheppard will miss multiple months. This is another significant injury the Pacers are dealing with in the backcourt after losing Tyrese Haliburton (knee) for at least two weeks.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Pacers head coach Rick Carlisle said Wednesday that T.J. McConnell (hamstring) is “doing better” and getting closer to a return to action.
body: McConnell has not played in a game this season due to a strained right hamstring. However, he is progressing in his recovery and passing some tests set by the Pacers’ training staff. McConnell could return to the court in a week or so, which is good news for a team that won’t have Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) for a few weeks.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Andrew Nembhard (neck) is available for Wednesday’s game against the 76ers.
body: Nembhard was initially listed as questionable with a neck injury, but he’s good to go against the 76ers Wednesday. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) sidelined for at least two weeks, Nembhard should have more playmaking responsibilities as the Pacers’ starting point guard.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Pacers coach Rick Carlisle told reporters Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) will miss at least two weeks.
body: Carlisle relayed to reporters that Haliburton is dealing with a mild left hamstring strain. He said Haliburton is considered week-to-week, though he won’t play for the next two weeks before being re-evaluated. It’s not great news for Haliburton, but it certainly could’ve been worse. Andrew Nembhard will likely see the majority of starts at point guard while Haliburton is sidelined.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Aaron Wiggins (knee) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Heat.
body: Wiggins is good to go after being listed as probable on the Hawks’ initial injury report. He’s averaging nearly 16 points per game so far, so managers in deeper leagues may get value from rostering Wiggins while he’s performing well.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: HoopsHype’s Michael Scotto reports the Lakers have signed Lawson Lovering to a two-way contract. Lovering spent time with the Grizzlies last season and even made a start for them. However, most of his time will likely be spent in the G League.
body: To clear the spot, they subsequently waived AK Okereke
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Ziaire Williams (foot) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Clippers.
body: Williams is dealing with left foot soreness and will miss Wednesday’s matchup with the Clippers. Jake LaRavia and Quentin Grimes are candidates to move into the starting lineup and see more minutes with Williams sidelined.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Luka Dončić (back) has been ruled out against the Clippers on Wednesday.
body: Dončić will miss the second leg of the Lakers’ back-to-back, which means Austin Reaves should be the focal point of the offense. Quentin Grimes or Collin Sexton will likely replace Dončić in the starting unit, with both taking on extended roles.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Justin Champagnie underwent surgery on Wednesday to repair a fracture in his right foot.
body: Champagnie had already been ruled out for Wednesday’s game, but he’s now on track to miss a lot more time than that. Bilal Coulibaly should be the primary reserve wing behind AJ Dybantsa when he moves into the starting unit, which could be as early as Wednesday night with him slated to make his NBA debut.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Tarik Biberović (heel) has been ruled out against the Thunder on Wednesday.
body: Biberović is technically a rookie, though he was drafted with the 56th pick in 2023. He hasn’t made his NBA debut yet, and it will wait at least one more game, though he likely won’t have much of a role when he is finally made available.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Santi Aldama (knee) has been ruled out against the Thunder on Wednesday.
body: Aldama’s season debut will have to wait at least one more game, but the combination of him being listed as doubtful ahead of this one and being assigned to the G League for a practice is a good indication that his return isn’t far off.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Tobias Harris (calf) has been ruled out against the Jazz on Wednesday.
body: Harris still hasn’t made his debut for the Spurs, which means the starting lineup should remain the same. It’s unclear how or if Harris’ eventual debut will impact San Antonio’s starting lineup, but it could push either Dylan Harper or Devin Vassell to the bench.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Jose Alvarado (ankle) has been ruled out against the Bulls on Wednesday.
body: This will be a third straight absence for Alvarado. Miles McBride and Tyler Kolek should continue to split the backup point guard minutes, which hasn’t been enough time for either to make a significant impact in the box score.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Naji Marshall (illness) is doubtful to play against the Thunder on Wednesday.
body: Marshall is now expected to miss a second straight game with this illness, which opened the door for Sergio de Larrea to take on extra minutes prior to his exit with a knee sprain and for Walter Clayton Jr. to play a role after that. Clayton should be able to play a few extra minutes off the bench with Marshall likely out.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Marcus Smart (forearm) has been ruled out against the Bucks on Wednesday.
body: Smart will miss a third straight game, though reports indicated that head coach Ime Udoka was “hopeful” that Smart would return for this game. His next opportunity to suit up will be in Dallas on Friday, while his absence will allow Bogdan Bogdanović to continue to take on extra minutes off the bench.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Jordan Poole (illness) is available to play against the Nuggets on Wednesday.
body: Poole was initially probable for this game but has now been cleared to suit up against Denver. He’ll continue to be a source of offense for them off the bench, but his role has been too small for him to be worth rostering outside of deep leagues.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: ESPN’s Shams Charania reports Tyrese Haliburton is set to miss time after being diagnosed with a left hamstring strain.
body: Haliburton was already questionable for Wednesday’s game, but he won’t be available for it. There is no clarity to this timeline currently, so hopefully head coach Rick Carlisle will provide more either before or after their game against the 76ers. Andrew Nembhard (neck) is questionable, and T.J. McConnell (hamstring) hasn’t played this season. Nembhard will likely be the starting point guard until Haliburton returns, with Quenton Jackson as the next man up. Rookie Braden Smith could also be part of the rotation if Indiana ends up truly shorthanded.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Yaxel Lendeborg (foot) participated in shootaround ahead of Wednesday’s game against the Timberwolves.
body: Lendeborg is still listed as questionable, but this is a good sign. The rookie has been fantastic early on and should continue to put up gaudy stats, assuming he’s available for this game. If something changes, Golden State could turn to Georges Niang in the starting unit.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Isaiah Joe (hip) has been ruled out against the Hornets on Wednesday.
body: Joe will miss a second straight game after landing hard on his hip on Sunday. Kevin Huerter and Ronald Holland II should continue to take on a couple extra minutes off the bench with Joe sidelined once again.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Ausar Thompson (ankle) is probable to play against the Hornets on Wednesday.
body: Thompson played on Tuesday after missing Sunday’s game, and he should be good to go for the second leg of this back-to-back. Daniss Jenkins, who started in place of Thompson on Sunday, should continue to play a reserve role.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Aaron Wiggins (knee) is probable to play against the Heat on Wednesday.
body: Wiggins was initially listed as questionable, but he is now expected to suit up against Miami. He has been a valuable piece off the bench for the Hawks so far this season and should continue to play a significant reserve role, where he has averaged 15.8 points per game this season.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: AJ Dybantsa (ankle) will play against the Cavaliers on Wednesday.
body: After missing Washington’s first four games of the season, Dybantsa will finally suit up for the Wizards. Assuming the ankle responds well to playing, he should make his home debut on Friday. Washington has already played this cautiously, so don’t expect Dybantsa to play 35 minutes immediately. He’ll likely be on a minutes restriction, and he may even come off the bench. Eventually, he’ll replace Bilal Coulibaly in the starting lineup, which could happen on Wednesday.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Simone Fontecchio (illness) has been ruled out against the Hawks on Wednesday.
body: Fontecchio was initially listed as doubtful for this game and has now officially been sidelined. He has played a grand total of six minutes this season and didn’t see the floor in either of Miami’s last two games, so his absence won’t alter the team’s rotation.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Anthony Black (personal) missed shootaround ahead of Wednesday’s game against the Raptors and is listed as questionable to play.
body: The expectation is that Black will be back with the team to play, but they’re still listing him as questionable. With Jalen Suggs (knee) set to miss a couple weeks, Black has a chance to start if he suits up tonight. If something changes, Jase Richardson, who is already starting, should take on more minutes. Tristan da Silva could enter the starting unit, with Franz Wagner taking on the point guard duties.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: ESPN’s Anthony Slater reports there is “an extreme level of pessimism” that Kristaps Porziņģis (illness) will play for the Warriors again.
body: Porziņģis is already considered “out indefinitely”, and there doesn’t seem to be any positive update coming soon. There really isn’t much clarity here, but the report indicates that sources in the team aren’t planning on Porziņģis suiting up for them again, and they could use his salary in a trade. If he plays this season, regardless of who it’s for, he should be productive. However, it doesn’t seem likely, so he can be dropped to the waiver wire.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Sandro Mamukelashvili accounted for 17 points (6-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, one block and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
body: Mamu delivered excellent production off the bench for the Lakers in the first half of Tuesday’s game, scoring 13 points in 12 minutes. Unfortunately, he wasn’t as effective after halftime, scoring four points on 2-of-4 shooting. Although Tuesday was a tale of two halves for Mamukelashvili, his ability to score points in bunches makes the forward/center worth rostering in 14-team leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Austin Reaves tallied 26 points (8-of-13 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), four rebounds, seven assists and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
body: Reaves, whose point total increased in each of the Lakers’ first three games, has scored 23+ points in all four outings. He didn’t record any defensive stats on Tuesday, but most fantasy managers target Reaves for his offensive production. Efficient against Portland, the Lakers guard didn’t turn the ball over at all in his 39 minutes. Reaves is shooting 63.3 percent from the field over four games, an incredible percentage given his place in the Lakers’ pecking order and how much attention opposing defenses pay him.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Luka Dončić amassed 41 points (12-of-22 FGs, 11-of-13 Fts), five rebounds, nine assists, one block and six three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
body: One game removed from dropping 52 points on the Jazz, Dončić had another prolific scoring night on Tuesday. In addition to the high field-goal percentage, he kept the turnovers in check, committing only two. Despite averaging nearly six turnovers per game, Dončić has been one of the most valuable players in nine-cat formats. Shooting 87.5 percent from the foul line, which represents significant improvement, certainly helps.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Robert Williams III finished Tuesday’s win over the Lakers with 14 points (6-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 10 rebounds, one assist, two steals and one block.
body: The Time Lord doesn’t need to log many minutes to offer solid fantasy value, as his Tuesday performance shows. Williams played 21 minutes off the bench and recorded a double-double with three “stocks.” As a result of his play throughout the victory, Williams was on the court in crunch time while starter Donovan Clingan (nine points, 10 rebounds, one assist, one block and two three-pointers in 26 minutes) was on the bench. Williams remains a deep-league option at best, but that could change with a few more performances like Tuesday’s.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Damian Lillard tallied 21 points (5-of-12 FGs, 7-of-11 FTs), five rebounds, four assists and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Lakers.
body: After comfortable wins over the Suns and Kings, we got our first “Dame Time” moment of the 2026-27 season on Tuesday. Lillard’s three-pointer with 43.1 seconds remaining extended Portland’s lead to six, essentially ending the game. He scored 10 of his 21 points in the final quarter, and he and Deni Avdija accounted for 19 of the Blazers’ 34 points in the frame. It’s still early in the season, but so far Portland’s perimeter rotation hasn’t hurt Lillard’s fantasy value.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Deni Avdija finished Tuesday’s win over the Lakers with 23 points (8-of-15 FGs, 3-of-7 FTs), four rebounds, nine assists, one steal and four three-pointers.
body: After scoring 11 first-half points on Tuesday, Avdija went quiet in the third quarter, scoring two points on 1-of-4 shooting. But he was front and center when the Trail Blazers needed him most, recording nine points, two rebounds, four assists and two three-pointers in the fourth quarter. Thanks in part to Avdija’s stellar play, the Trail Blazers outscored the Lakers 34-26 in the fourth and moved their record to 3-0.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jrue Holiday recorded 22 points (8-of-12 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Lakers.
body: After totaling 20 points in Portland’s first two games, Holiday had his most productive night of the season on Tuesday. The veteran guard played 30 minutes off the bench, and his minutes have increased in each of Portland’s three games. Thirty minutes may be Holiday’s cap, not because of health, but because of Portland’s perimeter depth. Starters Damian Lillard and Ja Morant also played at least 30 minutes, with fellow reserve Scoot Henderson logging 17.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ja Morant accounted for 23 points (9-of-13 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), four assists and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Lakers.
body: Sure, the Trail Blazers have played only three games, but they haven’t had any issues with how they distribute offensive responsibilities. Morant, Damian Lillard and Deni Avdija can all operate on or off the ball, and that was a huge factor in their win over the Lakers. While Morant took a back seat in the fourth quarter, he scored 10 of his 23 points in the first. With good percentages and a low turnover rate, he’s been close to a top-50 player in nine-cat formats so far.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Duncan Robinson finished Tuesday’s loss to the Knicks with 12 points (4-of-14 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers.
body: Robinson entered Tuesday averaging 19.7 points and 5.0 three-pointers per game. The Knicks focused more on him defensively, and the Pistons’ wing had a rough night. Robinson shot 0-of-8 from the field in the first half and missed all six of his three-point attempts. He got a couple to fall in the second half, but the final return wasn’t what fantasy managers hoped for.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cade Cunningham amassed 19 points (7-of-18 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), nine rebounds, eight assists, one block and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Knicks.
body: Given Cunningham’s scoring trend in Detroit’s first four games, he’s likely to score 20+ against the Hornets on Wednesday. The Knicks kept him in check for most of the night, with Cade totaling 10 points in the final three quarters of Tuesday’s defeat. The good news for fantasy managers was that he put up quality rebound and assist numbers, finishing one board and two helpers shy of a triple-double.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Paul Reed tallied 22 points (9-of-12 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), nine rebounds, three assists, two steals, one block and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s loss to the Knicks.
body: Making a second consecutive start for the injured Jalen Duren (hamstring), Reed was hot to start Tuesday’s game. Shooting 5-of-6 from the field, he was responsible for 13 points, three rebounds, three assists, one steal and one blocked shot in the first quarter. Unfortunately for Reed and the Pistons, he went quiet in the second and third quarters, totaling one less foul (four) than points (five) in those periods. As long as Duren’s out, Reed is a must-roster player in fantasy leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: OG Anunoby produced 13 points (5-of-15 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, two steals, two blocks and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Pistons.
body: The scoring output was limited, but Anunoby’s complete stat line should benefit category-league managers. Over four games, he’s shooting 38.8 percent from the field, which has hurt OG’s fantasy value. But he’s close to being a top-100 player, and Anunoby provided top-50 fantasy value in each of his first two full seasons in New York. He’ll be fine.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Karl-Anthony Towns accumulated 27 points (12-of-21 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 20 rebounds, three assists and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Pistons.
body: Towns’ only negative on Tuesday was his seven turnovers. He had a good night scoring-wise, and the Knicks’ center finished with his 17th 20/20 game, five of which have occurred since he was traded to New York. Towns was at his best in the third quarter, shooting 5-of-5 from the field and scoring 13 points. He’ll look to build on this showing when the Knicks visit the Bulls on Wednesday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Mikal Bridges notched 12 points (4-of-10 FGs), three rebounds, four assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Pistons.
body: While we aren’t going to proclaim Bridges “back” after a rough first week, Tuesday’s performance was much needed. He shot 4-of-8 from three against the Pistons, including 2-of-4 in the second quarter. New York outscored Detroit 26-12 in the period, rebounding from a slow start. Bridges can be a valuable fantasy option, but many managers were getting close to the point where they had to seriously consider cutting bait. Tuesday’s performance may buy him a little more time.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jalen Brunson recorded 23 points (5-of-18 FGs, 13-of-16 FTs), one rebound and seven assists in Tuesday’s win over the Pistons.
body: Ausar Thompson hounded Brunson for most of the night, which contributed to the low field-goal percentage. A busy night at the foul line boosted the point total, and the Knicks guard dished out seven assists, so Brunson gave fantasy managers some value on Tuesday. He’ll look to bounce back on Wednesday against the Bulls.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Mikel Brown Jr. amassed 17 points (5-of-17 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, five assists and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics.
body: Active after sitting out Sunday’s loss to the Pacers for injury management reasons, Brown played 28 minutes in Tuesday’s overtime defeat. With Egor Dëmin (leg) leaving in the second quarter and Nolan Traoré (cramps) in the fourth, Brown gained valuable crunch-time experience. His three-pointer with two-tenths of a second remaining forced overtime, but Brown also missed a couple of close-range shots in the extra period that proved costly. Overall, this was an encouraging night for the rookie, even with the outcome and the low field-goal percentage.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Nolan Traoré (cramps) finished Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics with 15 points (6-of-9 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), one rebound, three assists, two steals and one three-pointer.
body: Traoré got off to a good start on Tuesday, scoring 10 points in the first half. Unfortunately, he was relatively quiet after halftime and left the game in the fourth quarter with cramps. Over his last two games, Traoré has totaled 32 points, eight assists, three steals and two blocks. He was inserted into the starting lineup on Tuesday, and the results were encouraging. Traoré isn’t a must-roster player, but he’s worth adding to watch lists in deep leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Michael Porter Jr. tallied 27 points (8-of-16 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), 12 rebounds, two assists, two blocks and six three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics.
body: Porter shot 6-of-12 from three on Tuesday, bouncing back from a 0-of-5 effort in Sunday’s loss to the Pacers. He’s made at least four three-pointers in three of Brooklyn’s first four games, and that output is one reason MPJ has been close to a top-25 player through the season’s first week. Another challenging matchup looms, however, as the Nets host the Pistons on Friday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Egor Dëmin (leg) will not return to Tuesday’s game against the Celtics.
body: Dëmin suffered a right leg contusion during the second quarter of Tuesday’s game and returned to the locker room shortly thereafter. He’s now done for the night, with Keon Ellis entering the lineup to begin the third quarter.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Arizona Sports 98.7’s John Gambadoro reports that Oso Ighodaro (oblique) is feeling better but remains day-to-day ahead of Friday’s game against the Nuggets.
body: Ighodaro injured his oblique during the Suns’ season-opening loss to the Trail Blazers and has missed the last two games. While his absence hasn’t changed the starting lineup, as Khaman Maluach has been the preferred center, it has led to Duop Reath getting rotation minutes off the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Isaiah Joe (hip) is out for Tuesday’s game against the Knicks.
body: Joe landed hard on his right hip during Sunday’s win over the 76ers and did not return to action. His absence on Tuesday won’t affect fantasy basketball, as Ausar Thompson (ankle) is available.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ausar Thompson (ankle) is available for Tuesday’s game against the Knicks.
body: Thompson is back after sitting out Sunday’s win over the Knicks. He’ll take on the task of defending Jalen Brunson, while Daniss Jenkins returns to the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jaxson Hayes (shoulder) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Spurs.
body: Due to a sore right shoulder, Hayes did not play in Monday’s loss to the Grizzlies. If he can play on Wednesday, Hayes could start, as Jaren Jackson Jr. (knee) is out for 6-8 weeks. If Hayes can’t play, the Jazz would have to rely even more on Mo Bamba and Kyle Filipowski.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Nolan Traoré, Egor Dëmin, Michael Porter Jr., Julius Randle and Day’Ron Sharpe will start Tuesday’s game against the Celtics.
body: One game removed from recording 17 points and five assists, Traoré has been rewarded with his first start of the season. He replaces Keon Ellis, who will come off the bench. The change also means that Dëmin will spend more time off the ball, which could help him get going after a slow start to the season.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Derrick White (hip) is available for Tuesday’s game against the Nets.
body: White was initially listed as probable for Tuesday’s game, so the status upgrade was expected. He’ll fill his usual spot in the Celtics’ starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Anthony Edwards (knee) will undergo arthroscopic surgery and will miss up to two months.
body: So much for Edwards being listed as questionable on the Timberwolves’ initial injury report for Wednesday’s game against the Warriors. He’ll reportedly need to undergo an arthroscopic procedure on his right knee and could miss up to two months. While the timeline isn’t guaranteed, fantasy managers can stash Edwards on the IL until he’s cleared to return. As alternatives, Ayo Dosunmu and Terrence Shannon Jr. should see more opportunities, and starters Jaden McDaniels and Jonathan Kuminga should too.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Spencer Jones (hamstring) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Pelicans.
body: Jones hasn’t played this season, and his absence has factored into rookie Trevon Brazile getting consistent rotation minutes. While he isn’t a must-roster player in redraft leagues, Brazile has played well enough to merit remaining in the rotation once the Nuggets are whole.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cameron Johnson (ankle) is doubtful for Wednesday’s game against the Pelicans.
body: Johnson has missed Denver’s last two games and will likely miss a third. If he remains out, Bryce Hopkins should get another start.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Alpha Diallo (personal reasons) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Pelicans.
body: The good news is that the Nuggets are no longer listing a sprained right wrist as the reason why Diallo won’t play. However, he remains away from the team for personal reasons. With Cameron Johnson (ankle) doubtful, Bryce Hopkins is likely to get a third consecutive start.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Caleb Martin (thumb) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Thunder.
body: Martin hasn’t appeared in a game this season yet. However, if he is available on Wednesday, the Mavericks’ many injuries could thrust him into the rotation immediately. That wouldn’t be enough to make Martin a player worth rostering in fantasy leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Naji Marshall (illness) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Thunder.
body: Marshall did not play in Monday’s win over the Heat, but his absence coincided with Kyrie Irving’s return after sitting out Saturday. Irving is also questionable for Wednesday night; Marshall could start if he’s available, but Kyrie isn’t. If both can’t play, Walter Clayton Jr. and Marcus Sasser could see increased opportunities.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kyrie Irving (knee) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Thunder.
body: While Wednesday’s game is not part of a back-to-back, Irving is back on the injury report. After sitting out Saturday’s loss to the Spurs, he logged 33 minutes in Monday’s win over the Heat. Naji Marshall (illness) could potentially start if Irving can’t play, but he’s also considered questionable.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Sergio de Larrea (knee) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Thunder.
body: De Larrea sprained his right knee during Monday’s win over the Heat and did not return. Walter Clayton Jr. played 17 minutes against Miami and was productive; that may earn him rotation minutes again on Wednesday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Tarik Biberović (heel) is doubtful for Wednesday’s game against the Mavericks.
body: Biberović, the 56th overall pick in the 2023 draft, has yet to make his NBA debut. He has a slight chance of being available to play on Wednesday, but that wouldn’t affect fantasy basketball.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Santi Aldama (knee) is doubtful for Wednesday’s game against the Thunder.
body: Aldama has yet to make his Mavericks’ debut, and that may not change on Wednesday. However, the doubtful tag is a step in the right direction for the 7-footer, who was assigned to the Mavericks’ G League affiliate earlier Tuesday.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Anthony Edwards (knee) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Warriors.
body: Despite dealing with a sore right knee, Edwards played 41 minutes in Monday’s overtime loss to the Cavaliers. Minnesota has another back-to-back on Friday/Saturday, so Edwards may get a day off at some point. If so, Ayo Dosunmu and Terrence Shannon Jr. would take on larger roles.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Jaren Jackson Jr. suffered a torn MCL in Monday’s matchup with the Grizzlies, and he will be sidelined 6-8 weeks.
body: The good news for JJJ is that he won’t require surgery, but given his injury history, it’s another significant blow to his outlook for the rest of the season. With Jusuf Nurkić (foot) still sidelined, Jaxson Hayes is a guy to scoop up off the waiver wire as one of Utah’s only healthy centers.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Sixers reporter Kyle Neubeck reports that VJ Edgecombe was a full participant in Tuesday’s practice.
body: Edgecombe sat out Sunday’s matchup with the Pistons, but his full participation in practice suggests he could return as soon as Wednesday against the Pacers. If Edgecombe is forced to miss another game, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope could remain in the starting lineup.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Paul George and Mitchell Robinson are not on the injury report for Tuesday’s matchup with the Nets.
body: Both players took the court on Monday, and both are on track to appear in both legs of a back-to-back set. Fantasy managers should still keep an eye on their statuses closer to tip-off to ensure neither are late scratches.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: NBA Insider Marc Stein reports that Santi Aldama was assigned to the Texas Legends of the G League to practice with the team as part of his return-to-play protocol.
body: Aldama underwent knee surgery in March and has yet to make his Mavericks debut, but his assignment to Dallas’ G League affiliate is an encouraging update to his status moving forward.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Kawhi Leonard will miss “a period of weeks” due to swelling in his left knee.
body: According to Shams, an MRI revealed no structural damage, but the Raptors are being cautious with the superstar and will keep an eye on his knee while ramping him back up. In his absence, Ja’Kobe Walter should see an increased role. Walter started on Sunday and finished with 22/4/2 with three “stocks” and five triples. Guys like Jamal Shead and Collin Murray-Boyles could also be in line for bumps in playing time, but Walter is the preferred add from a fantasy basketball perspective.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: DeMar DeRozan accounted for 21 points (7-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, two steals, one block and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.
body: For the first time since his rookie season, DeRozan is being asked to come off the bench. As expected, the veteran forward needs to adjust to the unfamiliar role. After taking 19 shots in Denver’s first two games, he took 15 against the Warriors and recorded his first 20-point stat line of the season. As DeRozan gets more comfortable in his role, his chances of providing the fantasy value managers have grown accustomed to over the years improve.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Bryce Hopkins finished Monday’s loss to the Warriors with 13 points (5-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer.
body: Monday’s start was the second in as many games for Hopkins, who continues to fill in for the injured Cameron Johnson (ankle). Unlike Saturday’s win over the Pelicans, when he offered limited production, the rookie was more aggressive on offense. The result was Hopkins’ first double-figure scoring night as an NBA player. He should remain a starter until Johnson is healthy enough to play.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jamal Murray notched 19 points (8-of-13 FGs), six rebounds, eight assists, three steals and three three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.
body: After going off for 42 points in Saturday’s win over the Pelicans, Murray cooled off a bit on Monday. However, he still shot well; the final line reflected lower shot volume and his inability to get to the foul line. After attempting 13 free throws against New Orleans, Murray didn’t attempt any against the Warriors. Monday’s outcome aside, Murray’s gotten off to a good individual start this season.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Nikola Jokić recorded 19 points (8-of-18 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), seven rebounds, 11 assists, one steal, three blocks and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.
body: Two nights after recording a triple-double in Denver’s comeback win over the Pelicans, Jokić posted a double-double on Monday. The three-time MVP finished with a complete stat line and committed one turnover, a good start to the week for those rostering him. However, the Nuggets are now 1-2, and they needed to erase a large deficit to get that lone win. Simply put, Jokić needs more help from teammates not named Jamal Murray.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Brandin Podziemski recorded 18 points (7-of-14 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), seven rebounds, five assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Nuggets.
body: Back in the lineup after sitting out Saturday’s loss to the Suns, Podziemski recorded his second 18-point game of the season. He played 33 minutes against the Nuggets, a positive sign given the back issue that kept Podz out of the Warriors’ October 21 season opener. Golden State has three more games in Week 2, ending with a Sunday/Monday back-to-back, so another injury management night could be on the horizon for Podziemski.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Stephen Curry accounted for 24 points (8-of-8 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, two steals and three three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Nuggets.
body: For just the second time in his illustrious career, Curry finished a game without missing a shot. After making his lone attempt during the first half, the Warriors guard shot 7-of-7 from the field in the second half as they pulled away from the Nuggets. Given Yaxel Lendeborg’s play, the Warriors didn’t have to rely as much on Curry. If that continues, it would make the future Hall of Fame guard’s job a little easier.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Yaxel Lendeborg finished Monday’s win over the Nuggets with 31 points (9-of-19 FGs, 12-of-13 Fts), 12 rebounds, six assists, one block and one three-pointer.
body: On a night when Stephen Curry attempted just one shot in the first half, Lendeborg had his best game as a pro. The rookie forward recorded his second double-double in four games and his first 30-point stat line. Given Lendeborg’s role with the Warriors and how much the team seems to trust him, he could be one of the best rookies in fantasy basketball this season.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Mo Bamba started the second half and finished with 14 points (7-of-8 FGs), seven rebounds, one assist and four blocks on Monday against the Grizzlies.
body: Both Jaren Jackson Jr. (knee) and Lauri Markkanen (wrist) exited early from this game, which allowed Bamba and Josh Green to start the second half. Green wasn’t productive, but Bamba made the most of the opportunity. If Jackson remains out against the Spurs on Wednesday, Bamba may be in line to start. However, it is unlikely be produces to this level again, and the matchup against Victor Wembanyama isn’t ideal.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Ace Bailey recorded a double-double on Monday with 17 points (6-of-10 FGs), 10 rebounds, three assists, three blocks and three three-pointers against the Grizzlies.
body: Bailey has been excellent over Utah’s last two games, posting a double-double in both. However, his production could continue to climb. Lauri Markkanen (knee) and Jaren Jackson Jr. (knee) both exited early from this game and could remain sidelined. Bailey already moved into the starting unit after opening night, but his usage will continue to increase if Utah is missing two starters. He’ll look to stay hot against the Spurs on Wednesday.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Aaron Gordon was ejected from Monday’s game against the Warriors with 8:34 remaining in the fourth quarter.
body: Gordon was given two technical fouls in quick succession after arguing a call, ending his night with 8:34 left in the fourth quarter. He finished with seven points (2-of-10 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and one steal. Marvin Bagley III replaced Gordon in the lineup after he was ejected.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Keyonte George led the Jazz with 26 points (9-of-17 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), three rebounds and six assists in a 110-105 loss to the Grizzlies on Monday.
body: It wasn’t enough to get the win, but George was the most productive scorer in this game. Both Lauri Markkanen (wrist) and Jaren Jackson Jr. (knee) exited early, which meant more offensive responsibility for George. If either, or both, misses time moving forward, George’s usage will continue to skyrocket. He has been excellent to start the year and will look to stay hot against the Spurs on Wednesday.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Ty Jerome struggled on Monday but still contributed 15 points (4-of-15 FGs), one rebound, eight assists, one steal and one three-pointer against the Jazz.
body: After a scorching start to the season, Jerome fell back to earth in this game. His shot simply didn’t fall at the same rate, though he made up for it by dishing out a season high for assists. Jerome has been unreal to start the season, but it was never likely that he would maintain that pace. However, he should be a fantastic fantasy option for the rest of the season and one of the best value picks in fantasy basketball.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Cedric Coward recorded a double-double on Monday with 16 points (6-of-12 FGs), 11 rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers in a 110-105 win over the Jazz.
body: Coward has gotten off to a strong start in his second season, especially over his last two games, where he has recorded a double-double in each. It was an ugly win, but Memphis is now 4-0 to start the season. Coward has been a big part of that and is currently a top-50 player in fantasy basketball. He’ll look to keep it going in Portland on Thursday.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Jabari Smith Jr. recorded a double-double on Monday with 16 points (6-of-13 FGs), 12 rebounds, five assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers against the Hawks.
body: Smith has gotten off to a strong start to the year, headlined by a 30-point performance in the season opener. This was his first double-double of the year and a new season high for assists for Smith, and he only has one subpar outing this season, which came against the Spurs. He was held to seven points, though he only took five shots and added two steals and two blocks. Smith has been fantastic this year, which has been a big reason for Houston’s early success.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Alperen Şengün led the Rockets with 29 points (11-of-15 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), nine rebounds, nine assists, six steals, one block, one three-pointer and six turnovers in a 120-110 win over the Hawks on Monday.
body: Şengün has been fantastic to start the year, and this was one of his best performances. He fell just shy of a triple-double, but it was the steals that made this performance special. He set a new career high for swipes, which helped offset the turnovers. Şengün has taken a leap forward, and if he continues to produce to this level, the Rockets will continue their winning ways. Next up on the schedule is a trip to Milwaukee on Wednesday.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Onyeka Okongwu posted a full line on Monday with 11 points (5-of-10 FGs), nine rebounds, one assist, two steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Rockets.
body: To put it mildly, it has been a rough start to the year for Okongwu. This was his best performance of the year as he posted season highs in points, rebounds and steals. That isn’t saying much, but his lack of minutes has been the biggest concern. Only one game was impacted by a blowout, but he is currently averaging 4.5 fewer minutes per game that what he saw last season. Unless that changes, he won’t be able to make as much of an impact as he did last year.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: CJ McCollum lit up the Rockets with 20 points (8-of-16 FGs), one rebound, three assists, three steals and four three-pointers on Monday.
body: McCollum has been a solid source of offense for the Hawks since they traded for him last season. So far this year, his production has been underwhelming, but this ended up being his best scoring performance of the season. He has been efficient as a scorer, but the lack of volume has prevented him from making much of an impact for fantasy managers. Still, as a starter, he’ll continue to produce standard-league value.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Caleb Wilson recorded 17 points (7-of-15 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, one steal, two blocks and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Celtics.
body: Monday’s matchup was tough for Wilson, as the Celtics rolled out a lineup led by Jayson Tatum and Paul George. However, the rookie forward finished Monday’s defeat 6-of-10 from two and managed to do a little bit of everything in his 32 minutes on the floor. The Bulls may be 1-3, but Wilson’s start to the season has been encouraging overall.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Norman Powell tallied 20 points (5-of-11 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), one rebound, two assists, four steals and four three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Celtics.
body: Powell’s shot fell at a higher rate than it did during the opening week, with the veteran guard shooting 34.1 percent from the field in Chicago’s first three games. A bonus for fantasy managers was four steals, bringing Powell’s total to 10 over four games. He’s averaged at least one steal per game each of the last two seasons, so Powell managers may get a little more value in that category.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Josh Giddey finished Monday’s loss to the Celtics with 11 points (4-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), one rebound, four assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer.
body: After shooting a combined 7-of-26 from the field in Chicago’s first three games, Giddey was more accurate on Monday. Unfortunately for him and the Bulls, that didn’t keep them from getting blown out in Boston. Overall, Giddey’s final stat line wasn’t great, but those rostering him can’t ignore that he shot better than in Week 1.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Brandon Miller led the Hornets with 39 points (15-of-28 FGs), six rebounds, one assist, three steals, two blocks and five three-pointers in a 110-103 win over the Wizards on Monday.
body: The volume has been there all season, but the shots finally started falling for Miller in this game. That allowed him to set a new career high for scoring and score at least 30 points for a second straight game. Until Kon Knueppel (hamstring) and Coby White (calf) return, Miller is going to see as many shots as he wants. He has taken 57 shots over Charlotte’s last two games and should continue to see an insane amount of usage on offense, with a trip to Detroit up next on the schedule on Wednesday.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Kyshawn George lit up the Hornets with 20 points (8-of-14 FGs), four rebounds, two assists, one block and two three-pointers on Monday.
body: George came alive late for Washington and ended up scoring at least 20 points for a second straight game. He was limited by foul trouble, but he was able to step up late, which included scoring 11 of his 20 points in the fourth quarter on 5-of-6 FGs. George has seen his offensive role expand with AJ Dybantsa (ankle) still yet to make his debut. George will likely see fewer shots whenever that happens, though he should still be able to impact the game in other ways.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Trae Young recorded a double-double on Monday with 22 points (10-of-20 FGs), six rebounds, 10 assists and one three-pointer against the Hornets.
body: The NBA’s assist leader failed to record a double-double for the first time this season on Saturday, but he was able to get back on track in this one. He has also scored at least 20 points in every game this season, and he only needed one free throw to do get there in this game after averaging 11.7 attempts through their first three games. He should get back to that free throw rate moving forward, with the Cavaliers up next on the schedule on Wednesday.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Alex Sarr finished with 12 points (4-of-6 FGs), six rebounds, one assist and two blocks against the Hornets on Monday.
body: It has been a rough start to the season for Sarr, but he has progressed as a scorer every game. However, that isn’t saying much. He was held to single-digit scoring in each of his first two games and only had 10 points in the game before this one. He has five blocks over their last two games, which is really the only positive aspect of his season. He has only played 24.4 minutes per game, which could be correlated to his offseason foot injury. That’s just speculation, though it would help justify his limited role to start the year.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Alex Caruso (ankle) will not return Monday vs. Suns.
body: Caruso went to the locker room with an apparent ankle injury after Dillon Brooks accidentally fell on him. The Thunder are already dealing with injuries in the guard position, so it’s worth monitoring over the next few days.
author: Shawn Robinson

headline: Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski, Yaxel Lendeborg, Gui Santos and Draymond Green will start Monday’s game against the Nuggets.
body: Curry, Podziemski and Green are back after sitting out Saturday’s loss to the Suns. The latter will start at center, which means Santos remains in the starting lineup. Brandon Williams, Will Richard and Graham Ike head to the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Anthony Davis led the Wizards with 29 points (11-of-22 FGs), 10 rebounds, one steal and three three-pointers in a 110-103 loss to the Hornets on Monday.
body: After two quiet games in a row, AD was finally back to producing how he did in the season opener. He had a total of 28 points across their last two games without recording a double-double in either. It wasn’t enough to get Washington a third win, but it was good to see AD get back to dominating. He’ll look to keep this going in Cleveland on Wednesday.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Tyrese Haliburton, Kelly Oubre Jr., Aaron Nesmith, Pascal Siakam and Jay Huff are starting against the Bucks on Monday.
body: Huff will start in place of Ivica Zubac, who may miss an extended amount of time with an ankle injury. Andrew Nembhard (neck) is also sidelined, which will allow Oubre to get the nod in his place.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jared McCain, Ajay Mitchell, Kenrich Williams and Isaiah Hartenstein will start Monday’s game against the Suns.
body: The Thunder have three new starters for Monday’s game, and two (McCain and Mitchell) could hold onto those roles for the foreseeable future. Cason Wallace (shoulder) and Jalen Williams (ankle/fibula) could miss the rest of the season due to injuries that require surgery. “Kenny Hustle” starts for Chet Holmgren, who is dealing with right patellar tendinitis.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ivica Zubac (ankle) with no timetable for return, but encouraging
body: Speaking with media on Monday, Pacers head coach Rick Carlisle said Zubac is doing better and walked into the arena without a boot, but will not rush the big man back. This is the same injury that held the 7-foot center out for some time last season. Jay Huff will continue to start in his absence.
author: Shawn Robinson

headline: Aaron Nesmith (hamstring) is available for Monday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Nesmith being able to play both games of a back-to-back so soon after missing time with a strained hamstring is encouraging. He’ll fill his usual role in the Pacers’ starting lineup, but the fantasy upside is limited.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Marcus Smart (forearm) is now day-to-day with strain.
body: Speaking to media ahead of the Rockets contest vs. the Hawks, head coach Ime Udoka says Smart is day-to-day, but is hopeful the guard will return to the lineup on Wednesday vs. the Bucks.
author: Shawn Robinson

headline: Rockets head coach Ime Udoka said he expects Steven Adams (calf) to “miss a week or two” after undergoing imaging on his calf.
body: Adams missed Saturday’s game against Atlanta and had already been ruled out for Monday’s rematch. However, it looks like he’s going to miss at least a few more games. Clint Capela filled out the backup center minutes on Saturday and should remain in that role over the next handful of games. Capela contributed two points, three rebounds and an assist in their last game against the Hawks.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Andrew Nembhard (neck) is out for Monday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Nembhard will sit out the second game of Indiana’s back-to-back with a stiff neck. His absence opens up a spot in the Pacers’ starting lineup, with Kelly Oubre Jr. being a potential replacement. Nembhard’s absence may also result in more minutes for Quenton Jackson.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cooper Flagg (shoulder) is available for Monday’s game against the Heat.
body: Flagg is good to go after a left shoulder injury suffered on Friday sidelined him for Saturday’s loss to the Spurs. His return will bump Zaccharie Risacher to the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Nic Claxton (hamstring) went through an individual on-court workout on Monday.
body: Claxton injured his hamstring in early October, missing the entire preseason and Chicago’s first three regular-season games. He completed an individual workout on Monday, and the hope is that the Bulls’ center can resume practicing with the team next week. Jalen Smith should remain the starting center until Claxton is healthy enough to play.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cooper Flagg (shoulder) a game-time decision vs. Heat on Monday.
body: Head Coach Dusty May said Flagg is expected to play Monday vs. the Heat, but it will be a game-time decision after suffering a shoulder sprain against the Pacers.
author: Shawn Robinson

headline: Cason Wallace will undergo surgery to to repair a left labrum tear.
body: Wallace had already been ruled out for Monday’s game following an early exit on Sunday, but it now appears the injury is going to keep him sidelined a while longer. The hits just keep coming for OKC, with Jalen Williams (leg) set to have surgery as well. Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain will both take on significant roles until Wallace and/or Williams return.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Maxime Raynaud (knee) to be re-evaluated in two weeks
body: The center has progressed well, but remains sidelined for at least another two weeks. Raynaud is recovering from a right patellar subluxation sustained on Oct. 10.
author: Shawn Robinson

headline: Karim Lopez (knee) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Jazz.
body: Lopez missed Sunday’s game against the Kings and is seemingly on the wrong side of questionable for Monday’s tilt with the Jazz. His likely absence won’t impact fantasy basketball, however.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Isaiah Stewart (ankle) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Jazz.
body: Stewart is questionable for Monday’s game with an ankle injury. If he can’t play, Quinten Post could see more minutes off the bench, though he isn’t worth rostering in fantasy leagues.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Alpha Diallo (wrist, personal) is out for Monday’s game against the Warriors.
body: No surprise here as Diallo was initially listed as doubtful. With Cameron Johnson (ankle) doubtful, Trevon Brazile is the preferred streamer from the Nuggets’ bench.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Nikola Topić (back) and Thomas Sorber (knee) are out for Monday’s game against the Suns.
body: Both Topić and Sorber are yet to appear in a game due to injuries. Neither is worth rostering outside of dynasty formats.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jaxson Hayes (shoulder) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Grizzlies.
body: Hayes is listed as questionable with shoulder soreness for Monday’s game against the Grizzlies. If he’s ruled out, Kyle Filipowski could see some bench minutes, but still isn’t worth rostering in fantasy leagues.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Nikola Topić (back) and Thomas Sorber (knee) are off the injury report ahead of Monday’s game against the Suns.
body: Topić and Sorber are off the injury report now. Neither has appeared in a game yet this year, so even with the Thunder missing players, the pair are still only worth rostering in dynasty leagues.
author: Nick Shlain
